name: Dienedione

lead: Dienedione is a 19-nortestosterone steroid sold as a bodybuilding prohormone, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone, for more muscle mass.

It is thought to act as a prohormone to dienolone, which is structurally close to trenbolone and activates the androgen receptor. It became a US Schedule III steroid on January 4, 2010. Published research is limited to doping control, notably in horses, and no human studies exist.

paras: It was taken orally as a supplement in bodybuilding circles before scheduling. No documented routine or timeline exists.
No human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US (Schedule III) and UK (Class C) and prohibited in sport.

angle.text: Dienedione was marketed as a trenbolone-type prohormone for muscle gain: the body is thought to convert it to dienolone, which activates androgen receptors. It was sold until scheduled in 2010, and no human studies exist.

lead: Dienedione (estra-4,9-diene-3,17-dione) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group that was never medically used. It is thought to be a prohormone of dienolone and was sold as a bodybuilding supplement, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone.[1]
It became a US Schedule III steroid on January 4, 2010 and is Class C in the UK.[1] The published research is about doping control, particularly in horses.[2][3]

paras: Dienedione is mainly an intermediate in the synthesis of trenbolone, mifepristone, ulipristal and dienogest. Organon patents from 1999 cover a synthesis route from a soy phytosterol-derived starting material.[1]
In the US it was sold as a supplement, and some products were seized in FDA enforcement action related to Bodybuilding.com in 2010.[1] It is prohibited in human and equine sport.[2]

A 2025 study in Drug Testing and Analysis reported that dienedione is detected in the urine of entire male horses and investigated whether it is endogenous in that species; Wikipedia summarises this as finding small natural production in intact male horses.[1][2] Further papers addressed doping control and hair monitoring in horses.[3][4]

timeline.event: Becomes a US Schedule III steroid.[1]
Study reports endogenous nature in male horses.[2]
